The 3rd Wisconsin built breastworks of earth and rails and threw down stone walls and fences in its front on the east bank of Rock Creek on 2 Jul before 18:00; the 27th Indiana line used rails, timber and stone.
The enemy held the original intrenched line and the stone wall on the night of 2 Jul.

flags: exact clock time open (B.8.2); forum "late morning" is unreliable

sub_claims.claim: Hays ordered the house and barn in his front burned; Smyth's brigade passed the order and the 14th Connecticut set them on fire in several places after removing its killed and wounded.
The burning came after the lull began at about 11:00 and before about 14:00 on 3 Jul (the cannonade); the barn still sheltered Confederate skirmishers and was cleared at 07:30 that morning.
The barn was a ruin by late afternoon of 3 Jul.
The "house and barn in our front" are the Bliss house and barn.
The fires were set with hay, straw and cartridge paper.

works.name: Rummel barn

sub_claims.claim: A large barn stood on the Rummel farm in front of the 2nd Pennsylvania Cavalry's skirmish line on 3 Jul.
Confederate dismounted troops (Jenkins' brigade of Stuart's cavalry, with other forces) held the Rummel house and barn area on the afternoon of 3 Jul and fired from it.
Pennington's and Randol's batteries put shell after shell into the barn "making it untenable"; the barn bore the marks of that fire when the 1914 volume was written.
Stuart's men cut loopholes in the barn planking.
The action at the barn took place in the afternoon of 3 Jul (about 14:00 onward; the fight at the farm ended at sundown with the Union line holding the Rummel buildings).
